sourceClaims.section: Check Physical and Environmental Conditions; Run Connectivity Tests from the Web User Interface; Radio Settings; Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR)
sourceClaims.supportedClaim: Power, cable attachment, link indication, obstructions/range and connectivity tests are distinct observations; radio settings and noise affect diagnosis.
limitations: Product troubleshooting context, not universal SNR or throughput guarantees. Do not import configuration recommendations, channel legality, security or service success into the toy profile.

sourceClaims.supportedClaim: SNR is a signal-to-noise power ratio; its dB value is ten times the base-ten logarithm of that ratio.
limitations: For compatible power measurements with one reference, subtracting dBm yields dB. No universal acceptable threshold follows from this definition.

method.text: Keep the earlier reading visible as history. After a configuration change, record what you expect, then explicitly measure before drawing a current conclusion.

workedStep.text: For the worked boundary card, −65 minus −85 is 20 dB. The supplied inclusive threshold accepts equality. This worked card does not create a notebook measurement.

solution.text: Compare the displayed actual SNR readings. If 25 dB became 13 dB, it decreased by 12 dB and the current supplied link is below 20 dB. Say whether your prediction matched; neither weather cause nor throughput follows. This is assisted practice with the same optional completion.

practiceExplanation: Worked source card, not a notebook observation: signal −65 dBm and noise −85 dBm give 20 dB SNR. With the supplied viable path and matching settings, this exactly meets the fictional inclusive 20 dB minimum. It does not guarantee throughput. Opening this card records worked assistance and cannot complete Channel Scout.
retryExplanation: Restore the radio configuration and required inventory captured when you entered this exercise. Keep clues, notes and hint history. Begin a new attempt; all retained old readings are historical and stale until measured again. After completion, retry still restores the original entry radio configuration and inventory while your earned optional completion remains recorded. Retry does not save.
exitExplanation: Close Channel Scout at your captured Observatory origin. Keep the actual radio configuration you currently selected and all recorded observations; an impaired link remains impaired. No teleport, refresh or save occurs. Ordinary preparation controls and the required inspection kit remain recoverable.
